ruleName: Ball Lost or Out of Bounds: Provisional Ball
title: Procedure When a Ball is Out of Bounds
question: Your ball crosses an out of bounds fence on the 8th hole. You find where it crossed and drop a ball there under one penalty stroke. What is the ruling?

choices.text: Correct only if a Local Rule is in place.
Incorrect under the Rules of Golf.
You must play a provisional ball.

explanation: Under the standard Rules of Golf, if a ball is out of bounds, the player must take stroke and distance relief by playing another ball from where the previous stroke was made, under penalty of one stroke. Dropping a ball at the point it crossed the boundary is not allowed unless a Local Rule specifically permits it.

juniorVersion.title: What To Do When Your Ball Goes Out of Bounds
juniorVersion.question: On the 8th hole, your ball goes over the fence and out of bounds. You went to where it crossed and dropped a new ball there, adding one penalty shot. Is this the right thing to do?

choices.text: Yes, that is the right way.
Yes, but only if the golf course has a special rule.
No, this is not allowed by the normal rules.
You have to play a provisional ball.

juniorVersion.explanation: If your ball goes out of bounds, the rules say you must take a one-shot penalty and play a new ball from the same spot where you hit the last shot. You are not allowed to just drop a ball where it went out, unless there is a special rule for your course.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: When your ball goes over fences or beyond white stakes, it’s outside the golf course.
A second ball you hit just in case your first ball might be lost or out of bounds.
This means you take a penalty shot and hit again from where you last played.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Remind golfers to watch for white stakes or fences that mark out of bounds. Show them where to play from if their ball goes out.
likelyMisconceptions: Some kids think you can always just drop a ball where it went out.
Some may not know what a provisional ball is.
